title: Fission yeast RPA-TERT-Tpz1TPP1 complex promotes telomere extension and suppresses telomere recombination.
authors: Moser, Bettina A; Points, Madeline; Agrawal, Sourav; Didier, Adam C; Mennie, Amanda K; Lim, Ci Ji; Xu, Yong-Jie; Nakamura, Toru M
one_liner_zh: 该文通过AlphaFold3建模和遗传学方法研究裂殖酵母RPA-TERT-TPP1三元复合物促进端粒延伸的机制，属于蛋白质-DNA互作（端粒酶与端粒DNA）的结构建模研究，但对象非典型TF-DNA体系，方法以结构预测为主，对TF-DNA互作建模有方法借鉴价值。
abstract: Telomerase maintains chromosome ends by extending telomeric DNA, yet how recruited telomerase becomes productively engaged remains poorly understood. Recent studies found that Replication Protein A (RPA) contributes to telomerase stimulation through interaction with TERT in humans and with the TPP1 ortholog Est3 in budding yeast, suggesting a direct role in telomerase activation. Here, we provide genetic and structural modeling evidence for a RPA-Trt1TERT-Tpz1TPP1 ternary complex that promotes telomere extension while suppressing recombination in fission yeast. Guided by results from genetic screen, followed by AlphaFold3 modeling and systematic mutagenesis of RPA, Trt1, and Tpz1, we identify four key interfaces supporting telomerase function: Ssb1RPA1-Trt1, Ssb2RPA2-Trt1, Ssb2RPA2-Tpz1, and the TEL-patch-mediated Trt1-Tpz1 interaction. Notably, Tpz1-R81, previously assigned as the TEL patch, instead contacts Ssb2 in the complex. Epistasis and suppressor analyses indicate that the newly identified RPA-Trt1 and RPA-Tpz1 interfaces collaborate with the Trt1-Tpz1 interface to allow telomerase activation after recruitment. Furthermore, comparative analyses using AlphaFold3 suggest that these interactions are likely conserved in budding yeast and humans. Collectively, these findings support a model in which RPA serves as an essential component of the active telomerase complex, coordinating TERT and TPP1-like factors to enable productive telomerase engagement.
abstract_zh: 端粒酶通过延伸端粒DNA来维持染色体末端，然而招募后的端粒酶如何被有效激活仍知之甚少。近期研究发现，复制蛋白A（Replication Protein A, RPA）通过与人类中的TERT及芽殖酵母中的TPP1同源物Est3相互作用，促进端粒酶刺激，提示其在端粒酶激活中发挥直接作用。在此，我们提供了遗传学和结构建模证据，支持在裂殖酵母中存在一个RPA-Trt1TERT-Tpz1TPP1三元复合物，该复合物促进端粒延伸同时抑制重组。基于遗传筛选结果，结合AlphaFold3建模及对RPA、Trt1和Tpz1的系统性突变分析，我们鉴定了四个支持端粒酶功能的关键界面：Ssb1RPA1-Trt1、Ssb2RPA2-Trt1、Ssb2RPA2-Tpz1，以及TEL补丁介导的Trt1-Tpz1相互作用。值得注意的是，先前被指定为TEL补丁的Tpz1-R81，在复合物中反而与Ssb2接触。上位性和抑制子分析表明，新鉴定的RPA-Trt1和RPA-Tpz1界面与Trt1-Tpz1界面协同作用，使端粒酶在招募后得以激活。此外，使用AlphaFold3的比较分析提示，这些相互作用可能在芽殖酵母和人类中保守。总体而言，这些发现支持一个模型，即RPA作为活性端粒酶复合物的必需组分，协调TERT和TPP1样因子以实现端粒酶的有效参与。
